subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion’s normal install default remain on a setup-proven official release until the upstream wizard-runtime repair is shipped, or should maintainers intentionally adopt a prerelease default after that exact artifact passes full setup proof?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes the supported release channel, and its own evidence establishes that the selected prerelease cannot currently complete the normal setup path without an external package substitution.

options.title: Retain a setup-proven default
options.body: Revert or split out the `2026.7.2-beta.2` LKG change now, preserving the Companion fixes while the upstream repair lands and an official artifact is proven.

options.title: Sponsor a future beta default
options.body: After an official beta includes the upstream repair, approve the prerelease policy explicitly and require a clean exact-artifact setup, reconnect, and MXC proof before changing the default.

recommendation.title: Retain a setup-proven default
recommendation.body: Revert or split out the `2026.7.2-beta.2` LKG change now, preserving the Companion fixes while the upstream repair lands and an official artifact is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline routes this PR to this reviewer candidate and the unresolved choice is a release-default policy decision rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
